> 顏回見仲尼，請行。曰：「奚之？」曰：「將之衛。」

A student asks leave to go to a state whose ruler is young, headstrong, and careless with his people's lives. He intends to fix it. The master spends the rest of the chapter explaining why he will be killed.

人間世 is the chapter people skip because it sounds like office politics. It is the most practical chapter in the inner seven.

## 齋 is not fasting

齋: 齊也 — to gather, to still, to draw the mind in. Sacrificial fasting restricts the body and the diet. 心齋 empties something else: opinions, preconceptions, the case you have already prepared.

The chapter's answer to the student is not "try harder." It is: you are going in full. Full of a plan, full of what a good state should look like. Emptied, you might arrive.

## 虛 is a ruin

虛 is the original form of 墟 — an empty place, ground where a building once stood.

Not a dead silence. Space cleared of preconception, room left for the thing to arrive. 唯道集虛: the way gathers only in what has been emptied.

## 不得已: the hardest two characters in the book

不得已 is not "no choice," not "helpless," not the sigh of a man cornered by circumstance.

It is a timing word: the thing has already come to you, the moment has already arrived, and only then does a response arise. Not a campaign you launched; a response to what came. 感而後應.

The book adds a warning, because this word slides easily: slide one way and it becomes passivity; stiffen the other and it becomes forcing others to be like you.

## 材 and 不材

材: timber, usable material — the thing the world can take and use. The world prices usefulness. 莊子 points out what the price is: being useful is often the reason a thing gets cut down. 不材, useless, is the great use of lasting out one's years.

## 溢言: speech that overflows

溢: to brim over, to exceed the facts. Praise beyond what is true, blame beyond what is true.

The chapter says these are the most reliable producers of harm, because they arrive as goodwill. 溢言 is not a lie. It is a truth that has been inflated until the other person has to carry it.

## 蕩: shaken by a name

德蕩乎名 — virtue is shaken by name. 蕩 is to sway, to drift loose.

Virtue is settled on its own; the moment it lands on a name, it starts to sway, and swaying long enough, it scatters. 蕩 here is not "indulgence" — it is "being led by the name until the root is loose."

## 菑 is disaster, and the verdict is heavy

菑 — the character for 災, disaster. 菑人: one who harms people.

The judgment is aimed at the helper, not the tyrant: to impose benevolence on someone in the posture of saving them is, in this chapter's verdict, harm. The name for it is 菑.

## The test

What are you currently trying to fix in someone else, and with what plan? Then ask the chapter's two questions: did they ask, and have you emptied the plan before arriving? 不得已 is not a reason to do nothing. It is a reason to check whether you were invited.
